## 2026 primary defeat

The May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]] reports that Massie lost his Republican primary in Kentucky's 4th Congressional District to Trump-backed challenger [[ed-gallrein|Ed Gallrein]], a former Navy SEAL, in what the source calls the most expensive U.S. House primary in history. President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] endorsed Gallrein, campaigned in the state, and repeatedly attacked Massie on social media as "a bad guy" and "an obstructionist and a fool." Massie had positioned himself as an independent "[[america-first|America First]]" voice who opposed some Trump priorities, including certain foreign aid votes and tax legislation.

In his concession speech, Massie told supporters chanting "no more wars" and "America First" that lawmakers must follow the Constitution over party loyalty, and hinted at a possible 2028 presidential run. Badlands commentator [[ghost-of-based-patrick-henry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] argued the defeat would persuade reluctant Republicans to align with the [[israel-lobby|Israel lobby]], writing that "if Thomas Massie can't beat the Israel lobby in a fake election, nobody can." [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] described widespread "libertarian rage" online following the result.

## Kentucky primaries and the 2026 industrial mobilization

The May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]] documents several strands of Trump's activity. In Kentucky, his endorsement, campaigning, and social-media attacks helped [[ed-gallrein|Ed Gallrein]] defeat Representative [[thomas-massie|Thomas Massie]] in the most expensive U.S. House primary in history, while his endorsed candidate [[andy-barr|Andy Barr]] won the Republican nomination for an open Senate seat — outcomes the Brief presents as evidence of a tightening grip on the Republican Party.

The same issue reports Trump's Beijing summit with [[xi-jinping|Xi Jinping]], immediately mirrored by [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]]'s own visit, and administration talks with automakers including [[ford-motor-company|Ford]], [[general-motors|GM]] and [[oshkosh-corporation|Oshkosh]] to convert civilian capacity into defense output. In Middle East policy, Trump's pause of planned renewed airstrikes on [[iran|Iran]] — undertaken at the request of Gulf allies — was assessed by Israeli analyst [[raz-zimmt|Raz Zimmt]] as strengthening Tehran's incentive to resist U.S. demands. Badlands commentators read these threads together as a deliberate strategy: [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] as the mandate for "American Acceleration," and [[ghost-of-based-patrick-henry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] as a "perpetual holding pattern that allows neither peace nor war to break out," concluding that Trump intends to make peace with Iran.

## Beijing visit and the 2026 alliance analysis

The May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]] reports Putin traveling to Beijing to meet [[xi-jinping|Xi Jinping]] directly on the heels of [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] doing the same. Summarizing the [[center-for-european-policy-analysis|Center for European Policy]], the Brief notes that the Putin–Xi relationship has been assessed as evolving beyond a tactical "marriage of convenience" into a mature alliance rooted in a "shared consciousness," with nearly 50 leader-level meetings since 2012 and the February 2022 "no limits" friendship declaration issued days before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The analysis holds that Beijing has sustained Moscow's war effort with dual-use exports, coordinated information operations, and economic lifelines. [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] instead placed Putin within a [[sovereign-alliance|Sovereign Alliance]] with Trump and Xi, waging the [[multipolar-alliance|Multipolar War]] against what he calls the Hegemon rather than against one another.
entities/xi-jinping.md:
## 2026 Beijing summits

According to the May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]], [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]] traveled to Beijing to meet Xi immediately after [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] had done so. The [[center-for-european-policy-analysis|Center for European Policy]] argued that the Putin–Xi partnership had matured into a genuine alliance grounded in a "shared consciousness," noting that the two leaders have met nearly 50 times since 2012 — more than any other world leader has met Xi — and that both powers back [[iran|Iran]] while pursuing a vision privileging state power over individual liberty and seeking to reorder the international system against the West. [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] read the summit sequence as the cover story for a coordinated pivot toward sovereign, decentralized national development.
entities/iran.md:
## Negotiating position after the 2026 strike pause

The May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]] summarizes analysis by [[raz-zimmt|Raz Zimmt]] of the [[institute-for-national-security-studies|Institute for National Security Studies]] holding that Iran gained incentive to resist U.S. demands after President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] paused planned renewed airstrikes at the request of Gulf allies. Tehran was said to have concluded that Washington and its partners fear the fallout of renewed war more than Iran does, and that Trump's statements are unreliable — leading Iran to refuse concessions on its nuclear enrichment infrastructure and to seek upfront guarantees including a full end to the conflict, sanctions relief or unfrozen assets, and arrangements recognizing Iranian control of the [[strait-of-hormuz|Strait of Hormuz]]. The same Brief notes that both Russia and China back Iran, and that [[ghost-of-based-patrick-henry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] believes Trump intends to make peace with Tehran.

The May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]] links Israeli interests to two American and international developments. Domestically, the [[lankford-rosen-antisemitism-bill|Lankford–Rosen antisemitism bill]] drew commentary from [[ghost-of-based-patrick-henry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]], who argued its expected bipartisan majorities demonstrate that "Israel controls our Congress" and that the bill functions as a vehicle for dismantling the [[first-amendment|First Amendment]].

Internationally, the Brief recounts Finance Minister [[bezalel-smotrich|Bezalel Smotrich]] accusing the [[international-criminal-court|International Criminal Court]] of seeking arrest warrants against him and other members of the [[benjamin-netanyahu|Netanyahu]] government, calling such acts declarations of war and explicitly declaring war on the [[palestinian-authority|Palestinian Authority]] — in the commentator's reading, effectively declaring war on the [[united-nations|United Nations]] and the world. The same issue reports Israeli analysis from the [[institute-for-national-security-studies|INSS]] concluding that Trump's pause of airstrikes strengthened [[iran|Iran]]'s hand.

## 2026 suspension of the Permanent Joint Board on Defense

The May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]] reports that the United States suspended participation in the [[permanent-joint-board-on-defense|Permanent Joint Board on Defense]], the bilateral consultation body with Canada established in 1940. [[elbridge-colby|Elbridge Colby]], Under Secretary of Defense for Policy, cited Canada's failure to make "credible progress on its defense commitments." Canada had recently met [[nato|NATO]]'s 2 percent of GDP target with $63 billion in investments for ships, F-35s, submarines, and Arctic infrastructure, and pledged 3.5 percent by 2035, but U.S. officials considered this insufficient. Tensions were compounded by Prime Minister [[mark-carney|Mark Carney]]'s [[world-economic-forum|World Economic Forum]] address declaring the U.S.-led global order over. Analysts described the pause as symbolic, with [[norad|NORAD]] modernization, intelligence sharing, and border security continuing. [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] endorsed a harder line, writing that "Canada represents the global regime on our northern border" and that a more hostile posture "should be welcomed."
entities/mark-carney.md:
## Role in the 2026 U.S.–Canada defense dispute

The May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]] cites remarks by Prime Minister Carney — including his [[world-economic-forum|World Economic Forum]] address declaring the U.S.-led global order over — as part of the backdrop to the American suspension of participation in the [[permanent-joint-board-on-defense|Permanent Joint Board on Defense]]. [[elbridge-colby|Elbridge Colby]] announced the pause citing [[canada|Canada]]'s lack of "credible progress on its defense commitments," despite Canada's $63 billion in new investments meeting [[nato|NATO]]'s 2 percent target and its pledge to reach 3.5 percent by 2035. Commentators noted the puzzling timing, since the Davos speech had occurred months earlier; [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] speculated that intervening negotiations had failed.

## May 2026 statement on the ICC

The May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]] reports that Smotrich released a recorded statement accusing the [[international-criminal-court|International Criminal Court]] of seeking an arrest warrant against him and other members of the [[benjamin-netanyahu|Netanyahu]] government. He characterized such acts as declarations of war to which [[israel|Israel]] would respond appropriately, and explicitly declared war on the [[palestinian-authority|Palestinian Authority]], promising new actions. [[ghost-of-based-patrick-henry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] read the statement as effectively declaring war on the [[united-nations|United Nations]] and thus on the entire world, calling it "the raving of a lunatic" and "the behavior of a wild animal that has been backed into the corner," and arguing that Smotrich was committing Israel to continued conflict regardless of American policy.

The May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]] documents two Department of Defense actions. Under Secretary of Defense for Policy [[elbridge-colby|Elbridge Colby]] announced via social media that the department — referred to in some reports as the Department of War — was pausing participation in the [[permanent-joint-board-on-defense|Permanent Joint Board on Defense]] with [[canada|Canada]] "to reassess how this forum benefits shared North American defense." Separately, Defense Secretary [[pete-hegseth|Pete Hegseth]] described administration efforts to convert idle civilian manufacturing capacity — in talks with [[ford-motor-company|Ford]], [[general-motors|GM]] and [[oshkosh-corporation|Oshkosh]] — as placing the industrial base on a "wartime footing" amid stockpiles depleted by conflicts across Eurasia.

entities/burning-bright.md:
## Commentary in Badlands Brief 311

In the May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]], Burning Bright argued that the convergence of Russia and China in the central narrative grants [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] "the mandate he needs for a new era of American Acceleration." He framed the Trump–[[xi-jinping|Xi]] Beijing summit and [[vladimir-putin|Putin]]'s mirrored visit not as great-power rivalry but as "the ultimate cover story — the perfect translation layer" for a shared push toward a decentralized, sovereign and abundant future, describing the process as "more translation and actuation than preparation."

He read [[ford-motor-company|Ford]]'s WWII-style mobilization language as the revival of [[detroit|Detroit]]'s Arsenal of Democracy for "sovereign power projection along kinetic, technological and energetic axes," and characterized the [[multipolar-alliance|Multipolar War]] as one that Trump, Putin and Xi only pretend to wage against each other while actually waging it against the Hegemon. Protectionism and pragmatism, in his account, are "national-level disguises" over strategic nationalist competition; the [[sovereign-alliance|Sovereign Alliance]] "has inverted the script," and the "European Collectorate is being summarily exposed as feckless and weightless."

In the May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]], GhostofBasedPatrickHenry contributed two segments. On the [[lankford-rosen-antisemitism-bill|Lankford–Rosen antisemitism bill]] he wrote that he had predicted the development for three years, calling the measure "the Trojan Horse that will dismantle the [[first-amendment|First Amendment]]" and forecasting the widest bipartisan support since the Patriot Act — support he treated as proof that [[israel|Israel]] controls [[congress|Congress]]. He cited [[tim-burchett|Tim Burchett]]'s dismissal of concerns about Israeli influence and [[thomas-massie|Thomas Massie]]'s defeat as evidence that "nobody is coming to save you," urging readers to "become defiant... become undomesticated... become ungovernable."

On Israeli analysis of [[iran|Iran]]'s leverage, he argued that the [[israel-lobby|Israel lobby]] is losing patience with Trump, who "has brilliantly locked us into a perpetual holding pattern that allows neither peace nor war to break out." He described pro-Israel advocacy as failing because its tactics — fearmongering, condescension, and claims of eternal victimhood — mirror those of the Left, the NeoCons, academia's "cultural marxism," and the Woke movement, and pointed to [[bezalel-smotrich|Bezalel Smotrich]]'s ICC statement as the behavior of a cornered animal. He concluded that "President Trump intends to make peace with Iran."

## May 2026 restatement

The May 20, 2026 [[badlands-brief-311|Badlands Brief]] contains one of [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]]'s most explicit statements of the concept: "The Sovereign Alliance—Trump, Putin and Xi—has inverted the script." Writing amid [[vladimir-putin|Putin]]'s Beijing visit mirroring [[donald-trump|Trump]]'s own summit with [[xi-jinping|Xi Jinping]], he argued that what looks like escalatory posturing between a 'New Axis' and a fading Hegemon "is the precise mechanism cultivating the mass public mandate required for the pivot," and that the more dramatic the headlines, the more permission populations grant their leaders to reorient industry, capital and technology toward sovereign ends. He added that in this process "the European Collectorate is being summarily exposed as feckless and weightless."
